events.title: PAN 25/00552/PAN agreed by Fife Council (per APRS)

description: EIA screening request for the proposed data centre at Camilla Farm/Auchtertool, submitted 10 November 2025 after two extensions to the screening timetable (including a NatureScot consultation).
decision_notes: Fife Council concluded under the Town and Country Planning (EIA) (Scotland) Regulations 2017 (Schedule 2 discretion) that predicted effects were not significant enough to require EIA. The decision was strongly criticised (community council 'appalled'; MSP Mark Ruskell 'unfathomable'); Environmental Rights Centre Scotland advised a credible legal basis for challenge. This remains the historical council decision, but Scottish Ministers later directed on 17 August 2026 that EIA is required; see separate DPEA case EIA-250-002.

events.title: Screening opinion issued: EIA not required

planning_authority: Scottish Government Planning and Architecture (DPEA register)
description: Scottish Ministers' Environmental Impact Assessment screening direction for the Cato data centre proposal, linked to Fife Council planning permission in principle application 26/01243/PPP at land north of Camilla Road, Gleniston, Auchtertool.
decision_notes: DPEA records the case as decision issued. Consideration concluded on 17 August 2026 with a direction that an EIA is required. This later ministerial direction supersedes the practical effect of Fife Council's 1 April 2026 no-EIA screening opinion without erasing that historical local decision.

events.title: EIA screening direction case received by Scottish Government Planning and Architecture
Scottish Ministers issue direction: EIA required

description: Planning permission in principle for a data centre campus (Class 6) comprising data hall buildings, gatehouses and associated infrastructure, Land To The North Of Camilla Road, Gleniston, Auchtertool. Applicant listed on portal as Mr Greig Templeton; press and council statements identify the applicant company as ILI Cato Limited. 1,651 documents on the portal.
decision_notes: Status 'Registered' as of 3 September 2026. Portal neighbour-consultation expiry 24 July 2026; council confirmed all representations received by 24 July 2026 will be considered. The portal then recorded 'Environmental Assessment Requested: No', reflecting the council's screening position. Scottish Ministers subsequently directed on 17 August 2026 that an EIA is required (DPEA EIA-250-002).

representations.notes: 1,200+ objections published on the portal at the 24 July 2026 deadline; the council reported 14,000-16,000 total representations received, with ~10,000 documents processed for publication. Objection/support split not yet published. SEPA lodged a holding objection requesting further flooding information. Petitions: 8,000+ signatures against the development; 2,500+ for a Scottish moratorium on hyperscale data centres. The 1,200 figure is a published minimum.
